name: performance

findings.message: The change adds two new `find plugins/ -maxdepth 3 -name manifest.yaml` traversals (lines 167 and 237) that scan the same directory tree already traversed by the pre-existing line 109 and by `eb_compose_known_types` internally, totalling four identical filesystem scans per test run; a single scan whose results are stored in an array would serve all three sections.

Section 6 (SPEC-2) calls `eb_manifest_events` once per plugin inside the loop (one awk fork per manifest, ≈44 forks) despite section 5 having already read every manifest's events in a single batched awk call (line 170); the per-plugin events needed for section 6 could be derived from the already-collected data without re-parsing.

`find ... -exec dirname {} \;` (semicolon form) spawns a separate `dirname` process for each of the 44 manifests found; `find -printf '%h\n'` or bash `${m%/*}` parameter expansion would avoid all 44 forks with no semantic change.

The SPEC-1 loop (lines 184–191) forks a `grep -qxF` process for each engine event (≈80 events) to check membership in the plugin-namespace list; a single `grep -Fxf <(echo "$_1951_plugin_ns")` or an awk membership test would reduce this to one process for the whole check.

The SPEC-2 inner loop forks a `grep -qE` process for each declared event in each plugin (≈44 plugins × ~3 events ≈ 130 grep forks) to match a fixed regex; the regex could be applied to the full per-plugin event list in one grep call, or replaced with a bash `[[ $event =~ $RE ]]` test that avoids forking entirely.

The namespace extraction loop (lines 175–178) appends to `_1951_plugin_ns` with `+=` on each iteration; bash string concatenation is O(N²) in total copying work across N iterations — for the current ≈200 plugin events this is negligible, but is technically quadratic and would grow if plugin counts scale.

reason: the performance lens found no high or critical problem the change introduced that fails it
